native_metadata.implementation: independent engineered C++17; grouped live-only skiplist
notes: Times include queue construction/destruction, distance allocation, predictor queries and all queue work. All methods except direct_heap include the common pending map. Model training/build and correctness checks are excluded.
Observed counters are compiled out of timed runs. Queue multiplicities and size fields remain algorithm state.
One observed warmup per method, shuffled; each repetition has matched height seed and shuffled method order.

Same scalar distance to LIFO vertex map for queue ablations. direct_heap embeds vertices with reverse insertion sequence, preserving LIFO ties without the map. Reference oracle uses an independent vertex-tie pair heap.
Guided set and bitmap share the same grouped skiplist and live-only rank buckets; plain skiplist shares grouping without rank buckets.
Grouping alters original artifact hint history and random-height consumption. This is an engineered crosscheck, not exact artifact reproduction.
Dense hierarchical bitmap is O(log_64 U), not vEB. Grouped heap controls duplicate compression. No RSS or total memory claim.
All three fitted advisors and training samples remain resident across methods; this is not isolated per-method memory measurement.
Training/build are measured once per invocation; baseline queues require neither. Shared-host timings are diagnostic.
native_metadata.training_timing_note: one common std_heap run, collecting every successful noninitial insertion; excludes graph read and oracle

protocol.applicability: radix included only when every target weight has integral value; scalar-double distances must remain exactly representable for integer workloads
protocol.baseline_semantics: lazy insertion and stale-entry Dijkstra semantics; direct_heap stores distance/reverse-insertion-sequence/vertex without a pending map for deployment comparison; std_heap shares the scalar-key/pending-map kernel for ablations; both preserve equal-distance LIFO order. Decrease-key benchmark results are not directly interchangeable without changing the update protocol.
protocol.job_order: one native process per graph/train/query case; seeded shuffle of all 42 cases
protocol.method_order: driver supplies a seeded shuffled list; native program must reshuffle every repetition and record order, with paired random-height seeds
protocol.oracle_policy: independent Python heapq reference plus parent/triangle certificate; native pair-heap oracle; compare little-endian IEEE754 binary64 distance arrays exactly outside timing

prior_art.relevance: established monotone integer radix-heap baseline; original decrease-key bound is not asserted for lazy reinsertion
prior_art.title: Faster Algorithms for the Shortest Path Problem

prior_art.relevance: established integer predecessor and bitmap-bucket engineering; not a novelty claim for our bitmap index
prior_art.title: Engineering Predecessor Data Structures for Dynamic Integer Sets

protocol.scope: native CPU engineering control; no new predecessor or radix algorithm claim; synthetic shifts are controlled stresses
protocol.shift_design: fit on training_graph (unshifted base), query target workload with frozen predictor
protocol.source_design: three fitted training models per target, first heldout near and first heldout far source from each frozen split; no source reselection

runtime.process_model: one subprocess per graph/train/query case, no concurrent workers
runtime.timing_owner: root-coordinated sequential native follow-up after Python timing/memory
